meta.session: arena/25418e3f-nba3 (official refresh 2026-11-14: 183-game result log, newest injury report, post-slate team ratings, availability timeline) on top of arena/8d3d0271-nba3 (engine, gates, leaderboard)
meta.as_of_note: Official pages were re-read on 2026-11-14 (UTC) at 09:45Z: newest injury report 11/14 04:15 AM ET, team statistics read after the 11/13 slate, results log through 2026-11-13 (183 games). Injury, tip-time and stat values move during a slate; re-read the official pages before acting. See the Report-availability page for which numbers are already stale and when each one settles.

engine.name: Walk-forward Massey margin model + shrunk scoring-environment totals model
engine.shrinkage: Ridge penalty and totals-shrinkage weight chosen by validating on the most recent 20% of PAST games only (select_hyperparameters).
engine.determinism: Seeded (seed 20261114); two consecutive runs produce byte-identical output, which is what makes the CI drift gate mean anything.

luck_test.method: Each rule simulated under its own fair-line null; the largest absolute edge on the board per iteration; 95th percentile reported as the luck threshold.

strategies.name: Fade big home favourites
strategies.rule: Mirror of ST-01: the same games, the other side.
strategies.tier_label: Rejected - not distinguishable from luck
strategies.verdict: FAILS - no evidence of skill

rows.pair: Home points vs away points (same game)
rows.note: Computed from the 183 official final scores. This is the number that decides whether a same-game side+total parlay is fairly priced as independent.
Out-of-sample residuals from the walk-forward run. The key input for pricing a same-game parlay that combines a side with a total. The interval includes zero, so independence is not rejected here.

rows.pair: Cover (vs our spread) AND over (vs our total), same game
rows.note: Joint hit rate 0.2214 vs 0.2351 under independence; dependence ratio 0.942. A ratio above 1.0 means the two legs land together more often than independent pricing assumes, which is how a book protects itself on same-game parlays.

availability.rule_quote: By 5 p.m. local time the day before a game (other than the second day of a back-to-back), teams must designate a participation status and identify a specific injury, illness, other medical condition, or other reason for any player whose participation in the game may be affected for any reason. For the second game of a back-to-back, teams must report the above information by 1 p.m. local time on the day of the game. In addition, teams are required to submit a game-day injury report between 11 a.m. and 1 p.m. local time (and between 8 and 10 a.m. for tip-offs 5 p.m. or earlier) on game days (besides the second game of a back-to-back).
availability.note_no_clock_conversion: Deadlines are published in local time, exactly as the rule words them. The offset between a venue's local clock and Eastern time is not printed on the official pages read for this project, so no ET equivalent is asserted -- that column is left blank rather than filled from memory.

availability.headline: Zero teams in the window are overdue. Every missing row is explained by a deadline that has not arrived yet: the five back-to-back teams on 2026-11-14 file by 1 p.m. local today, every 2026-11-15 team files by 5 p.m. local tomorrow's-eve, and no official report exists yet for 2026-11-16 or 2026-11-17. So a 3-day-ahead line is priced on ratings and rest alone, and the injury overlay can only be applied to the day it is filed for.

b2b_correspondence_1114.interpretation: On the 2026-11-14 slate the five teams whose rows are missing from the newest official report are exactly the five teams playing the second game of a back-to-back, whose report deadline is 1:00 PM local on game day. Their absence is a rule-driven timing gap, not a failure to file, and it closes hours before tip-off -- so these games are recoverable by waiting, not by guessing.

log_provenance.source_label: NBA.com official scoreboard, read 2026-11-14 after all nine games had finished (Final / Final/OT state printed).
verification: Official team advanced statistics (nba.com/stats/teams/advanced, read 2026-11-14T09:45Z) publish GP for all 30 teams; the extended log reproduces every one of the 30 GP values, and the 30 GP values sum to 366 = 2 x 183.
The same page's W and L columns (30 x 2 values, 183 wins and 183 losses) reproduce exactly from the extended log.
The post-game W-L record printed under each of the 18 teams on the scoreboard page matches the record recomputed from the extended log for all 18 team-records.
Independently, the official November calendar's per-date game counts (13 -> 9 GAMES, 12 -> 4, ...) plus the log's own October rows reach 183 games from a different page of the same site.
log_provenance.note: F36-03 predicted the log would reach 184 games. It reaches 183: the official GP column, the official W+L columns and the official per-date counts all give 183 games through 2026-11-13. The off-by-one in the hand-off note is recorded as flag 25418E3F-01 rather than quietly adopted.

superseded.reason: The ratings snapshot was read at 2026-11-14T01:05Z, while 11/13 games were still in progress, so 18 of 30 teams were one game stale. The injury overlay is the 11/13 07:45 PM ET report; the 11/14 04:15 AM ET report is newer and is checked against it row for row.

injury_delta.note: Every 2026-11-14 row of the 04:15 AM ET report matched the stored 07:45 PM ET report on status and reason. rows.pair: Home points vs away points (same game)
rows.note: Computed from the 183 official final scores. This is the number that decides whether a same-game side+total parlay is fairly priced as independent.
Out-of-sample residuals from the walk-forward run. The key input for pricing a same-game parlay that combines a side with a total. The interval includes zero, so independence is not rejected here.

rows.pair: Cover (vs our spread) AND over (vs our total), same game
rows.note: Joint hit rate 0.2214 vs 0.2351 under independence; dependence ratio 0.942. A ratio above 1.0 means the two legs land together more often than independent pricing assumes, which is how a book protects itself on same-game parlays.

rows.pair: Two legs in different games (cross-game parlay)

flags.item: After the refresh the totals model still loses to a constant out of sample: RMSE 19.449 vs 19.386 on 140 walk-forward games (the margin model wins: 15.945 vs 16.921). Every originated total is therefore weaker than the originated spread, and every totals rule on the board inherits that.

A table whose explanation is wrong is a defect even when every figure in it is right, so it is flagged rather than quietly rewritten.

review_findings.finding: Multiple independent model products report different samples, estimates, correlations and strategy statuses; none is designated as the reconciled source of truth.
review_findings.next_action: Do not combine or rank these results. Select one pipeline, define its data contract, and reproduce every result from identical timestamped inputs before publishing a canonical leaderboard.
review_findings.handling: Handled in this session: the canonical pages are built from one dataset (data/app/canonical.json) and from the official-sourced /origin/ pipeline only; the other workstreams are linked as snapshots and are not mixed in.

review_findings.finding: Several model inputs name secondary sources, including Basketball-Reference and ESPN, rather than showing an authorized official/licensed data chain. Rights and exact source snapshots are not demonstrated here.
review_findings.next_action: Source provenance is not proof of permission. Pause public derivative-use claims pending review of contracts/terms, versioned raw files, retrieval timestamps and redistribution rights.
review_findings.handling: Open. The canonical pages use official NBA inputs only; the Basketball-Reference/ESPN inputs remain in the /edge/ and /lab/ snapshots and are not published on the canonical pages.

review_findings.finding: Some published artifacts include betting prices and labels such as “POSITIVE EV,” even though the repository does not establish a licensed market-data source or common settlement specification.
review_findings.next_action: These are model outputs, not verified value. The source and rights must be established, odds timestamps and settlement rules recorded, vig/execution assumptions checked, and validation independently reproduced.
review_findings.handling: Open. The canonical pages publish no market price and no EV label; the /edge/ and /lab/ snapshots still do and remain flagged.

review_findings.finding: README has contradictory statements: it says no lines, correlations, picks or performance claims are shown, but elsewhere describes those outputs and separate sections document them.
review_findings.next_action: Replace with one versioned, consistent status report. Keep every experimental output clearly distinguished from an official fact and from a validated recommendation.
review_findings.handling: Handled in this session: the README now has one canonical section that states exactly what is published, what is derived and what is unverified.

review_findings.finding: Injury data are snapshots with different timestamps across sites; the official injury index says reports are updated continually. A past PDF is not a current slate feed.
review_findings.next_action: Store immutable report versions and timestamps; re-fetch the latest official report for every run; show staleness and suppress outputs if required inputs are missing. Do not infer minutes from status.
review_findings.handling: Handled in this session for the canonical pages (one snapshot, 11/13/26 07:30 PM ET, with the diff against the previous snapshot published). The earlier sub-sites still carry older snapshots.

review_findings.finding: Upcoming slates and picks are fixed November 2026 files; the official schedule document is explicitly subject to change. No automated current-feed refresh is demonstrated by the static Pages site.
review_findings.next_action: Use request-time schedule retrieval and a bounded 72-hour window; persist source time/version; suppress the slate on feed failure, schedule changes or stale snapshots.
review_findings.handling: Open. The published window is a dated snapshot with its source and retrieval time shown on every page; a request-time feed is proposed as a site improvement (CS-33).

review_findings.finding: Correlation outputs are not a shared, reconciled measurement. Different artifacts use different sample sizes, data sources, markets and possibly definitions.
review_findings.next_action: Keep values separate and unendorsed until pair definitions, sample construction, time windows, uncertainty, multiple-testing handling and source rights are harmonized and independently reproduced.
review_findings.handling: Handled in this session for the canonical pages: one correlation table, from one pipeline, with sample size, interval and status per row. The other artifacts remain unendorsed snapshots.

review_findings.finding: Passing local checks is not a line-by-line verification of every claim. Existing validators focus on specific generated sites/data schemas; they do not verify external truth, licensing, model quality or current URLs.
review_findings.next_action: Maintain site-specific tests, add scheduled source freshness checks and human review of changed source content; state exactly what each check proves.
review_findings.handling: Partly handled in this session: the canonical build states what it proves (row-level source link, link integrity, official-value cross-check) and the repository-wide screen is reproducible (scripts/scan_table_sources.py). External truth, licensing and model quality remain outside the build's scope.

review_findings.finding: NBA's Terms of Use text includes restrictions on NBA Statistics in connection with gambling activity and on certain regularly updated comprehensive-statistics databases without express prior consent.
review_findings.next_action: This is not a legal determination about the project. Obtain current terms review and written permissions/contract advice before using NBA-sourced statistics in any gambling-related service.
review_findings.handling: Open. Legal review is an owner decision; the canonical pages publish no betting recommendation and link the terms.

review_findings.finding: The intended product audience, offering model and compliance scope in the Netherlands are not defined.
review_findings.next_action: Get qualified Dutch counsel's assessment before deciding whether to offer information, picks or betting-related services to others; do not treat this page as legal advice.
review_findings.handling: Open. Tracked as an open question with the official regulator source.

review_findings.finding: Different sub-sites contain distinct inventories, ID namespaces and dates; the root dashboard previously said outputs did not exist, although they are present elsewhere.
review_findings.next_action: Use the root dashboard as the overview; label each sub-site's provenance and snapshot; reconcile IDs and remove obsolete contradictory summaries only after review.
review_findings.handling: Handled in this session: one canonical dashboard with one ID namespace; the earlier sub-sites are kept, labelled as snapshots and linked from the landing page.

review_findings.finding: The user's “remove luck” goal is not literally achievable; predictive evaluation can separate signal from outcome noise only probabilistically.
review_findings.next_action: Use proper probability scores, calibration, walk-forward evaluation, uncertainty intervals, pre-registration and prospective shadow results. Never claim luck-free outcomes.
review_findings.handling: Addressed in the canonical Method page: luck is kept out of the evaluation, not out of the outcome.

review_findings.finding: A mechanical scan across the repository's HTML files found table-body rows that lack a direct official NBA/Ksa link. Earlier measurement by session 2e50a71a: 1,521 rows scanned, 423 without a direct official link (389 excluding the archived research-dashboard.html). Second independent scan on 2026-11-14 (scripts/scan_table_sources.py): 2,111 rows in 90 files, 369 without a direct official-host link.
review_findings.next_action: This is a conservative automated screen, not a manual judgment that each row needs NBA evidence. For any row whose value cannot be confirmed from an official/authorized source, leave the value blank, label it unverified, and add an appropriate source before reuse. A full page-by-page source correction of the earlier sub-sites remains outstanding.

questions.question: Can picks or betting recommendations be published to people in the Netherlands?
questions.known: Not determined. Art. 1 of the Wet op de kansspelen prohibits promoting participation in unlicensed gambling (see S12). Ksa states that without a licence an operator may not advertise at all, and that online sports betting needs an Art. 31a licence (S10, S11). This is not legal advice. No picks are published.
questions.missing: Dutch counsel opinion on whether picks, tips or analysis count as promotion
questions.next_step: Obtain a written legal opinion. Until then, picks.html publishes blank cells and no picks

questions.question: How should a Probable or Available-with-injury row affect a line?
questions.known: Known: the engine counts Out and Doubtful as absences and treats Questionable as 'listed but not counted'; Probable and Available (9 rows on the 11/14 slate, e.g. Caleb Martin with a thumb splint, Nolan Traore with a calf) currently have no effect at all.

questions.next_step: Either state on the page that Probable/Available rows are ignored and why, or capture player game logs and measure how minutes actually shift for splint/mask cases. The first costs nothing.

review.item_reviewed: Defects found and fixed in the strategy engine during this build
review.finding: Four defects were found by reading the engine's own output rather than trusting it: (1) two-leg parlays were being scored against a 50% fair-line rate instead of 25%, which put a losing same-game parlay at the top of the first draft of the leaderboard; (2) the permutation test shuffled win flags within a date, which cannot change the total and so returned p=1.000 for every rule — it was replaced with a whole-board Monte Carlo against the fair-line null; (3) the 'high-octane' threshold used the median of the whole sample's projections, which is look-ahead — it now uses only prior projections; (4) an under-regularised Massey model printed a 28-point spread, so ridge and totals shrinkage are now chosen by validating on the most recent 20% of past games.
review.status: Irregularity — found and fixed in this session
review.recommended_action: Keep publishing defects found this way. A leaderboard whose top row is a bug is worse than no leaderboard.

review.item_reviewed: A signal that turned out to be the model's own error
review.finding: 'Fade the highest projected totals' posted 69.7% on 66 out-of-sample games (p=0.0019, q=0.016) before the totals model was regularised. After shrinkage toward the league mean it fell to 65.5% on 29 games (p=0.136). The apparent edge was our own miscalibration, not a property of NBA games. Published as flag NF-50 rather than as a finding.
review.recommended_action: Treat any bias found against our own line as a model defect to repair until a licensed price feed makes an external comparison possible (question CQ-40).

review.finding: The header comment documents an 8-column format (date, start_ET, away_team, away_pts, home_team, home_pts, OT, note) but every data row carries 5 fields, and the source named in the header is Basketball-Reference, which is not an official NBA property. The values themselves agree with the official capture, so this is a citation and schema defect, not a data error. review.item_reviewed: Unresolved merge conflict committed in the workflow file
review.finding: The base commit this branch started from (4e9dec4) contained literal '<<<<<<< HEAD', '=======' and '>>>>>>> origin/main' conflict markers inside .github/workflows/pages.yml, between session e40cd215's integration steps and the canonical capture steps. A workflow file with conflict markers is not valid YAML, so every CI run on that commit would have failed at parse time. main resolved it later; this session rebases onto that resolution and re-applies its own steps on top, so both sides' steps are present and no marker remains.
review.status: Irregularity — found and repaired in this session
review.recommended_action: Treat a committed conflict marker as a build failure: add a CI step that greps the tree for '^<<<<<<<' and exits non-zero. It is a one-line check that would have caught this.

review.item_reviewed: Injury capture miscounted the teams that had not filed
review.finding: scripts/capture_official_2026_11_14b.py set is_team_not_submitted by testing the Current Status column only. The official PDF prints 'NOT YET SUBMITTED' in the Reason column with Current Status blank, so all five such rows were counted as player rows: the published totals read 122 player rows and 0 not-submitted rows instead of 117 and 5. The counter is now computed from both columns, and the page states the split explicitly. The row-level cross-checks were never affected — they normalise both columns before comparing — which is why the defect only surfaced when the summary fields were read against the PDF rather than trusted.
review.status: Irregularity — found and fixed in this session
review.recommended_action: None. Keep publishing counts derived from the source columns rather than from a single assumed one.

review.item_reviewed: An engine swap tripped another session's CI drift gate
review.finding: integrate/engine.py (session e40cd215) derives its cross-engine reconciliation from the lines published in app/, so replacing the app/ engine changed its output and its 'git diff --exit-code -- data/integration/model.json' drift gate failed on this branch's first CI run. The engine is deterministic (verified byte-identical across runs), so the correct fix is to commit the regenerated artefact: data/integration/model.json, dash/data/model.json and dash/reconciliation.html. The comparison still reads 22 of 22 games agreeing on the favoured side; only the gaps moved (median 2.39 -> 1.77, max 4.76 -> 4.44, sd of app/ spreads 10.81 -> 8.81). Their gate did its job — it caught that an upstream input changed. Those three files are e40cd215's scope and their session is closed; they were regenerated rather than left failing, and the deviation is logged.
review.recommended_action: Session e40cd215: confirm the regenerated reconciliation, or make the comparison read from a pinned snapshot of app/ so an engine swap elsewhere cannot move it. Logged as CR-8D-06. Alternative considered and rejected: weakening the drift gate.

review.item_reviewed: Rebuilding the canonical engine invalidated another session's audit
review.finding: Session 36e18d83's audit36/check.py recomputes an 'engine agreement' block comparing the dash/ engine against the app/ engine and compares the result against values hard-coded in its own committed results file. This session replaced the app/ engine, so the recomputed figures moved (sd of app spreads 10.81 -> 8.81, median absolute gap 2.39 -> 1.78) and the check now reports one failure. The engines still agree on the favoured side in 22 of 22 games, so this is a stale expectation, not a new disagreement. audit36/ is that session's file scope and was not edited; its modified results file was reverted.
review.recommended_action: Owner of audit36/: re-run the audit and re-publish the engine_agreement block against the current app/ engine, or read the expectation from the build output instead of hard-coding it. Logged as CR-8D-04. The audit36 step is not in the CI workflow, so CI is unaffected.

requirements.how_addressed: Official schedule for 2026-11-14 to 2026-11-17 (27 games with game id, tip time, venue and city), official team advanced statistics for all 30 teams, official final scores for 183 games (2026-10-20 to 2026-11-13), and the official injury report 11/14/26 04:15 AM ET (49 rows: 26 player rows, 5 team rows NOT YET SUBMITTED for 11/14 and 18 for 11/15) - all captured and compared field by field with the values earlier sessions stored.
requirements.blocker_or_gap: Historical box scores and per-player game logs were never captured. Those two gaps block the most downstream work. See CQ-39 and NF-52.
requirements.verification_status: Captured 2026-11-14: 88/88 overlapping slate fields, 240/240 team-stat fields and 122/122 injury rows agree with the stored captures (scripts/capture_official_2026_11_14b.py). Re-read 2026-11-14 09:45Z by scripts/capture_official_2026_11_14c.py: six checks, all pass - 366 official team-games = 2 x 183, W and L columns 183/183, 18 scoreboard records, 31/31 injury rows stable, mid-slate staleness explained, slate counts 5/9/8/5

requirements.requirement_from_brief: Originate own NBA lines
requirements.how_addressed: Lines originated for all 27 games of the live window (re-originated 2026-11-14 on 183 games: all 27 lines moved, median 1.1 points, max 4.9) by a walk-forward Massey margin model with ridge shrinkage plus a totals model shrunk toward the league mean. Both shrinkage parameters are chosen by validating on the most recent 20 percent of past games only. Code: scripts/strategy_lab.py, seeded and deterministic.
requirements.blocker_or_gap: The margin model is only modestly better than a constant baseline and the totals model is worse than one. Both facts are published rather than hidden. See NF-49.
requirements.verification_status: 140 out-of-sample forecasts; margin RMSE 15.945 vs 16.921 baseline, total RMSE 19.449 vs 19.386 baseline

requirements.requirement_from_brief: Research and develop strategies that generate useful signals
requirements.how_addressed: 15 rules across single bets, same-game parlays and cross-game parlays, each scored out of sample against nine gates. Six are exact mirror pairs so the losing direction cannot be hidden, and one is a null control.
requirements.blocker_or_gap: No rule shows a signal that survives its own p-value, FDR correction and the whole-board luck threshold. See NF-51.
requirements.verification_status: Largest edge any rule posted is 18.0 pp; the luck threshold for a board this size is 31.2 pp

requirements.requirement_from_brief: Run as a leaderboard competition with rewards for top strategies
requirements.how_addressed: A ranked board with a composite skill score, five reward tiers (T1 funded to T5 blocked) and a stake allocation per tier. Zero rules are currently in T1 or T2, so nothing is funded.
requirements.blocker_or_gap: The reward schedule itself needs an owner decision: prize contest, pool, or internal scoring. Dutch rules treat these differently. See CQ-36.
requirements.verification_status: Statutory position read; no reward rule approved. A unit currently means a paper unit

requirements.requirement_from_brief: Single bets, parlays and player prop combos
requirements.status: Singles and parlays priced; prop combos blocked
requirements.how_addressed: 12 single-bet rules, 1 same-game parlay rule and 1 cross-game parlay rule are scored. Same-game cards for all 27 games and cross-game cards for the four dates are published with fair prices. Four player-prop combos are listed and all four are blocked.
requirements.blocker_or_gap: Prop combos need per-player game logs to measure the joint distribution. Without them every cell is blank by policy. See NF-52 and CQ-39.
requirements.verification_status: 4 of 4 prop combos published as BLOCKED with the unblocking step; no value invented

requirements.requirement_from_brief: Each strategy must pass validation gates
requirements.status: Gates defined and applied; nothing passes
requirements.how_addressed: Nine gates: provenance, look-ahead, sample size, power, significance, FDR, stability, economics at an assumed price, and the whole-board luck threshold. Every rule is scored against all nine and the per-gate grid is published.
requirements.blocker_or_gap: All thresholds are proposals this project has not had approved. Two further gates are proposed but not built: pre-registration (G10) and price reality (G11). See CQ-38.
requirements.verification_status: Exact binomial tests used, not a normal approximation; Benjamini-Hochberg applied across all 15 rules

requirements.requirement_from_brief: Determine correlation values
requirements.how_addressed: Home points vs away points (r=0.128, n=183 after the 2026-11-14 log extension), spread residual vs total residual (r=0.014, n=131), and the same-game cover-and-over joint rate with its dependence ratio are measured from official results. Four player-level pairs and the cross-game pair cannot be measured and are left blank with the reason printed in the cell.
requirements.blocker_or_gap: Player-level correlations need per-player game logs. The cross-game independence figure is printed as an assumption, not a measurement. See CQ-39.
requirements.verification_status: Values, sample sizes and 95 percent intervals published on the Correlations page; blanks flagged

requirements.requirement_from_brief: Remove luck; build selectively skill-based strategies
requirements.how_addressed: Exact binomial tests against the market's fair-line rate; Benjamini-Hochberg across the board; a 5,000-iteration whole-board Monte Carlo producing a 31.2 pp luck threshold; date-block bootstrap for return intervals; split-half stability; mirror pairs so the losing side is visible; and a null control that must fail. It does: 47.3 percent on 131 games, p=0.60.
requirements.blocker_or_gap: The methods detect luck; they cannot manufacture skill from 174 games. Nothing on the board beats the threshold. See NF-51.
requirements.verification_status: Null control ST-NUL fails 8 of 9 gates, which is the check that the gates work

requirements.requirement_from_brief: Generate picks for every upcoming slate up to 3 days ahead, using originated lines
requirements.how_addressed: One priced row for every one of the 27 games in the 2026-11-14 to 2026-11-17 window (today plus the maximum three-day horizon) with an originated spread, originated total, fair moneylines, projected score and availability status. Generated by a pipeline that reruns without manual input.
requirements.blocker_or_gap: These are our own fair prices against our own line, so their expected value is zero by construction. No market price is connected, so nothing here is a bet and no value is claimed. See NF-55 and CS-36.
requirements.verification_status: 27 rows, one per game; 2026-11-13 games excluded because they were live at capture time (NF-54)

requirements.requirement_from_brief: Track how injuries affect rotation minutes and production
